title: Willie Dixon's audition and meeting Little Brother
summary: She auditioned for Dixon, paid her own fare to Chicago, met Little Brother and the other musicians, and decided to go to London.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: So then they had Willie to come and interview me from Chicago. So they made Willie come. Then he said, "Well, let me hear you play some blues." So I played everything else but the blues and finally I played " Sam from Alabam." He say, "Oh, that's great." He say, "Now, I want some

real blues, Sippie, now." Said, "_______ Sam was good." I played "Sweet Georgia Brown," and I played "_______ Sam," then finally, I end up playing "Shorty George." I end up playing "Shorty George." He say, "Now, that's what I want." So he told me, said he was going to send me a ticket. Willie didn't send me a ticket. So I was so anxious to go on this job -- Vicki told me, said, "Sippie, you be sure you go." And so I got a letter from Willie and Willie told me to be in Chicago that Friday and he said (unintelligible). And so there was just -- the letter didn't come for me to go to Chicago, so then I -- the paper, I always read my horoscope and it said on them, "Use your own money to start with and show people that you are true, you can trust them." So I took the -- I just took that hunch and paid my own fare to Chicago and so when I'm in Chicago, this Little Brother come down to Willie Dixon's house and I was there. So I met Little Brother's wife -- not his -- yeah, Little Brother brought his wife with him and Willie Dixon, I met his wife, and I met his little children and everything. We all (unintelligible) barbecue sandwich and everything, got me a beer _______. His wife say, "Sippie, play a piece before you go." So then I say, "Well, Brother know I can play the blues." So finally I played "I'm a Mighty Tight Woman." So (inaudible) "That gal's all right," "That gal's all right." So Willie got the car and _______ didn't go to London. Now, you know, I was scared
See, Willie didn't go to London and I'm going by myself.
You went to London by yourself?
With the , you know. It was more me going myself, (unintelligible).

So Willie took me in the car and Little Brother was in the car and , he was a good drummer. He really was a good drummer. He played that drum and another -- Junior was -- played the harmonica, he went. It was some of us went and came from Louisiana and Big Billie (PHONETIC) come from Louisiana, you know.
But that was the first time you ever met Little Brother?
Yeah, all of them at the same time.
But isn't he an old Chicago piano player?
But you didn't know him in Chicago?
